title: The Minimum Viable Manager: Building Trust, Feedback, and Alignment
gist: Matt Gjertsen (Built, ex-SpaceX training lead) argues first-time managers need only three foundational skills—trust, clear expectations, feedback—and that AI raises rather than lowers the value of leadership skills because it makes every worker a manager of agents and amplifies the cost of misalignment.

themes.theme: AI raises the value of management skills

insights.claim: Gjertsen reports that for roughly 18 months companies disinvested in people and leadership skills amid doubts about needing people, but the conversation has turned and firms are realizing they still need people managers.
insights.speaker: Matt Gjertsen
insights.so_what: Signals a rebound in corporate L&D/leadership training spend after AI-driven pullback.
insights.quote: There was a lot of de-investment, disinvestment in the people skills, the leadership skills.

insights.claim: Using Elon Musk's vector-sum view of a company, AI increases each person's magnitude, making alignment of direction all the more critical.
insights.speaker: Matt Gjertsen
insights.so_what: As AI amplifies individual output, misalignment costs grow, raising the premium on strong leadership.
insights.quote: Their magnitude is going to go up, which means the alignment of them becomes all the more critical
